newsitem.title: FRANCE: Bancaire pleases with property clean out.
newsitem.headline: Bancaire pleases with property clean out.

text.p: Shares in finance and leasing house Compagnie Bancaire limited their fall on Wednesday in a sharply lower market, as brokers said they approved of a clear out of its property assets.
"The future is clearer from now and we can expect better profits thanks to the re-focusing on the core businesses," said one market operator.

Cie Bancaire eased 0.70 percent at 628 francs, while the market was down 1.66 percent. Paribas Capital Markets confirmed its buy recommendation, on a view that the 1996 profit was being hit at the expense of future profits.
The Paribas analyst reckoned Bancaire has potential to rise eight percent in relation to the market.
CCF Elysees Bourse upgraded the stock to a buy from lighten, while fund managers said research house Detroyat went to buy from sell on the basis of the clean-up of the accounts.
Dupont Denant considers that it was vindicated in its outperform recommendation, market sources said.

Cheuvreux de Virieu held its short-term buy(2) recommendation and considers the stock should benefit in the medium term from an easing in uncertainties over property markets. That should lead to a reduction in the stock's 22 percent discount to net asset value, they added.

Bancaire announced on Tuesday it was passing 2.5 billion francs in provisions for its Sinvim and UCB subsidiaries. That amount brings total provisions for property assets to 3.7 billion for this year.
It forecast a 1.2 billion franc net loss for the 1996 year due to the provisions. To offset the provisioning, it sold a six percent stake in its Cetelem subsidiary, making a one-billion capital gain.
